Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Model fit evals & benchmark links — Acme follow-up

Hi Sam & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Use case: customer-facing summary generation + ingest pipeline classification for support tickets (~100k monthly active users).
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms P95 on short summaries, ability to handle bursts up to ~500 TPS across the pool, and strict PII handling (need VPC/private deployment).

Recommended initial model candidates for evals (balanced latency + quality):
- redwood/llama-3-7b-instruct (quantized): lower cost, good for short summaries
- redwood/phi-13b-q4_k_m: higher quality on long-form summaries at modest latency
- open/model-x-70b-8bit (for high-quality long-tail cases; consider for Dedicated pilot)

I've exported our Redwood-verified performance profiles and a short prompt set we used for the benchmark. Highlights (full CSV attached and dashboard link below):
- Llama-3-7b-instruct (quantized): median latency 35ms/token, P95 = 180ms for 128-token outputs, sustained throughput ~550 TPS on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool (with batching)
- Phi-13b-q4_k_m: median latency 48ms/token, P95 = 260ms, sustained throughput ~220 TPS
- Model-X-70b (8-bit): median latency 120ms/token, P95 = 420ms, sustained throughput ~90 TPS

Notes / concerns:
- We saw a small quality regression on the phi-13b prompts on two prompt templates (examples in the attached CSV). We flagged these in the evals and included suggested prompt rewrites — we can iterate quickly and retest.
- For your P95 requirement under bursty traffic, we recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale + prefix KV caching to keep cost predictable.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_acme-20260302.csv (benchmark scores + per-prompt metrics), model_profiles_acme.pdf (verified performance profiles)
Dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-20260302
HubSpot: https://app.redwood.ai/deals/HUBSPOT-2026-00042

Suggested next steps:
1) Run a 24-48 hour smoke eval using your sample prompt set + our suggested prompts (we can run in hosted sandbox or on Dedicated trial).
2) Technical deep-dive with Alex to walk integration and prefix caching details (30-45m).
3) Security/compliance kickoff (we can drop in our SOC2 packet) — Priya suggested this.

Are you available for the tech deep-dive Thu 2026-03-05 10:00am PT? If not, propose two windows and we'll accommodate.

Thanks,
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifying Qs before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) For the Llama-3-7b numbers you listed, is the P95 measured end-to-end (including network + routing + batching) or just inference kernel? We need end-to-end P95 under 200ms for the shortest templates.
2) What does the throughput number assume for request concurrency and batching window? Our front-end bursts are spiky and often single-request-per-user.
3) Can you attach the prompt examples that showed the phi-13b regression? We want to review before the eval run.

Also, we'll need the procurement team to see a canary rollout plan and the SOC2 packet before we run anything on our side. Can you loop in security?

If Thu 3/5 10am PT works, we can take that. Otherwise Friday morning is fine.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Analytics
sam.patel@acme-analytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Model fit evals & benchmark links — Acme follow-up

Sam — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) P95 definition: the numbers in the CSV/dashboard are measured end-to-end from our API gateway through the inference runtime (includes routing + batching overhead) — these are Redwood-verified percentiles. The median/percentiles in the CSV include the distribution across concurrent clients.

2) Throughput assumptions: the sustained TPS figures assume a 8–12ms batching window on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with adaptive batching; for single-request spiky traffic we recommend enabling low-latency routing and smaller batching windows (you'll trade some unit cost for P95). We included simulated burst scenarios in the attached CSV (columns: concurrency_profile, observed_tps).

3) Prompt regression: attached a short sheet with the two failing templates and suggested rewrites (see model_profiles_acme.pdf, tab 2). We recommend trying the rewrite + a light temperature tweak; we can run those as A/B evals.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_acme-20260302.csv, model_profiles_acme.pdf
Security packet: https://app.redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf (we can add the full evidence package once NDA is in place)

I'll book the tech deep-dive for Thu 2026-03-05 10:00am PT with Alex (calendar invite forthcoming). Action items:
- Alex to share integration checklist + sample code for prefix KV caching
- Jordan to scope Dedicated pool sizing and cost estimate for your expected burst profile
- Marissa to circulate SOC2 summary and benchmark CSV to procurement

Thanks — looking forward to the session.
—
